verdict:
The new monitor plate works well as a corner-pin plate, but as a shot it fails. The other three frames have not changed since r2: window is still 21 % warm, desk has 31.6 % of pixels below 8/255, and letters 23.5 %. The code now holds r2's camera and trim fixes (commit 5b33108, 09:18). None of those frames has been re-rendered since then (they were committed between 05:09 and 05:27), and none of them contains the monitor.

The plate is technically clean. The raw panel is a flat emission at L 130.6 with std 0.47. There is no glare and no clipping (graded max 146). I re-measured the exported pins against the rendered edges on all four sides, and they agree within 0.2-0.5 px. All four corners survive an 8 % push about the frame centre. Nothing in it looks like lettering.

As a picture it does not read as Tim's desk:
- No desk is in frame. The desk top and the monitor's foot project below the bottom edge (the foot at about y 1010-1050), and the laptop lid hides the lower post. So the monitor seems to stand on the window stool. The housing's lower edge is about 5 cm above the 0.98 m stool (the panel's lower edge 7.6 cm), and from z 1.255 the two line up.
- None of Tim's things is visible: no wood, pad, letters or mug.
- Along the bottom edge (x 430-1010, y 640-720) is the laptop's lid, seen from its screen side. It is a dark slab (graded mean 13) with a lumpy lit edge, and it is a second screen.
- The lamp shows only as a black, unlit arm. Its lower joint touches the right bezel, with no gap at y 430-470. Its shade is a sliver cut by the top-right edge (x 1235-1280, y 60-200). No bulb, no pool and no warm light shows on any surface. A black spring arm next to a monitor reads as a mic boom.
- The grade leaves it cold. Of the lit pixels outside the panel, about 7 % are warm on the graded frame (29 % raw). The blank panel, a light-grey card (graded L 114, R-B -19), carries 76 % of the frame's light, and nothing visible around it shows that light.

Three things in the code make it cold:
- room_fill_colour has no 'monitor' entry, so room_fill runs at x8.0 in the default blue (0.6, 0.72, 1.0).
- The slat exclusion is applied only when name == 'window'.
- The camera looks at the side of the desk that the lamp's shade faces away from. Its light falls along (-0.6, 0.8), toward the pad.

The panel is also 29° off axis. Its right edge is 401 px tall against 515 px on the left, a 22 % keystone. That foreshortens the far side of whatever is pinned there; in the current EDL_v3, shot 03-15 puts page 1 of Tim's written CECC statement on this screen.

This needs a reframe that puts the screen on the lamplit desk. The laptop has to leave the frame: from the reframe its lid would stand just under the housing and hide the post and foot. The plate also needs a matte pass and a glass pass. Then it would be a fern-style "real media on a rendered screen" insert.
answers:
C54 Q1, does the cutaway read as a screen on Tim's desk? No. It reads as a blank monitor in front of a window in a cold room.
- No desk surface is in frame. I checked by exact projection, which reproduces the corners file to 0.1 px. The monitor's foot lands at about y 1010-1050 of 720, and the desk's back edge at about y 900.
- The laptop lid hides the lower post. So the monitor seems to rest on the window stool. The housing's lower edge is about 5 cm above the 0.98 m stool (the panel's lower edge 7.6 cm), and from z 1.255 they meet in the image.
- Nothing of Tim's is visible: no oak, pad, letters, mug or glasses.
- The only foreground is the laptop's lid, seen from its screen side, so it is a second screen. It is a dark slab along the bottom edge (x 430-1010, y 640-720, graded mean 13). When the image is brightened, its Tripo bezel edge looks lumpy.
- No published frame establishes the monitor at all. desk.jpg and window.jpg were committed at 05:09 and 05:27, and the monitor was added at 12:04.
- By projection, re-renders at the current cameras would show it:
  - in `desk`, as a dark sliver running off the left edge (visible to about x 87, y 145-770);
  - in `window`, at about x 510-757, y 218-391 of the 1920 frame.

Q2, do the lamp and blinds place it in the room? The blinds do: they are the same white slats as in `window`. But they are the cool element: the graded slats behind the top bezel are about L 56-58.
- The lamp does not. Only its black spring arm shows, plus a cut sliver of shade at the top-right edge. There is no lit shade rim, no bulb glow and no pool on any surface. By projection the bulb is at x 1392, off the right edge, and the lamp's base is below the frame.
- The arm's lower joint meets the right bezel with no gap at y 430-470 (x 951-1000), so the two dark silhouettes merge (graded 5-12). The arm alone reads as a mic boom or monitor arm, not a desk lamp.
- Measured on the graded frame: about 7 % of the lit pixels (L > 40) outside the panel are warm (R-B > 10). On the raw frame it is 29 %, so the grade removes what warmth there was.
- Causes in tim_desk.py:
  - apply_camera's room_fill_colour has entries only for desk and window. So for 'monitor', room_fill (trim 8.0) burns the default cool (0.6, 0.72, 1.0).
  - The slat exclusion from room_fill and night_glow is applied only for 'window'.
  - laptop_screen_light stays at 0.18.
  - The camera looks at the side of the desk the shade faces away from.

Q3, will the panel carry an insert cleanly? Mechanically yes. As a believable screen, not yet.
- Good:
  - The raw panel is a flat emission (L 130.6, std 0.47, max-min 3), with no glare, moiré or reflection to fight the insert.
  - The pins match the rendered 50 % edge crossings within 0.2-0.5 px on all four sides, with a 2-3 px anti-aliased edge.
  - Corners through a push about the frame centre stay inside. At 5 % they all stay well inside. At 8 % they land at TL (186, 45), TR (974, 68), BR (963, 502) and BL (204, 601), safe, while the housing's top lands about 17 px from the top edge.
- Problems:
  - The panel is 29° off axis, a 22 % keystone (right edge 401 px against 515 px on the left). Whatever is pinned there is foreshortened on its far side. In the current EDL_v3, shot 03-15 puts page 1 of Tim's written CECC statement (s1_p1-1.png) on this screen.
  - The grade's vignette darkens the panel. On the graded JPEG it falls from about L 128 at its centre to about 80 at its top-left. Composite onto the raw PNG and grade afterwards, or the insert will sit unvignetted.
  - The 1-2 px edge pixels already mix the light-grey panel with the bezel. Any insert darker than the panel, such as testimony video or a dark page margin, will show a faint light rim there. A rendered coverage matte avoids it.
  - Glare: there is none, and that is the realism problem. The panel is bare emission (mt.glow) with no glossy face, unlike the laptop's mt.screen. A real panel facing the lamplit room would carry a faint reflection of the lamp and the room in front of it. Without a glass pass the insert will look pasted on.
  - Light: the panel is a near-white page (emission 0.61 on (0.68, 0.75, 0.86), emission_sampling NONE). That brightness suits the planned insert, a white document page (s1_p1-1.png averages 242/255). Nothing visible in this frame faces the panel, because the wall, stool and blinds are all behind it, so its light cannot show here. Once a reframe puts oak in front of the foot, that oak must take the screen's light. With emission_sampling NONE and no area light in front of the panel, it will get little.
  - Depth of field: at f/5.6 focused at 0.836 m it runs about 0.78-0.90 m, while the panel spans 0.72-0.96 m. The near-left end of the bezel blurs by about 2.5 px and the far-right end by about 2 px, while a pinned insert will be uniformly sharp. Stop down to f/8, or defocus the insert's ends in the comp.

Does it still read as Tim's warm lamplit desk? No: it reads as one more of the film's cold rooms.

Stage, for scoring:
- `desk`, `letters` and `window` are the r2 frames, unchanged. The code already holds r2's camera and trim fixes (commit 5b33108: window lens 30 and exposure -1.3, letters at x -0.20 and lens 120, desk loc y 0.23), but the finals were not re-rendered.
- So the measured faults stand: window 21 % warm, desk 31.6 % below 8/255 with the claw hand, and letters 23.5 % below 8 with the black right band.

fixes.problem: The cutaway shows no desk, none of Tim's things and no lamp light, so the monitor seems to stand on the window stool. The laptop lid is a dark foreground slab. The lamp arm touches the right bezel, and the shade is cut at the top-right edge. The panel is 29° off axis, a 22 % keystone.
fixes.fix:
Reframe nearly frontally from behind the chair's left side, and include the desk and the lamp:
- CAMERAS['monitor'] = dict(loc=(0.42, 0.95, 1.40), aim=(0.42, -0.12, 1.03), lens=30, focus='fx_monitor', fstop=8.0, beat='ch09', exposure=-1.0, cast=False).
- Keep the chair empty. Tim's left shoulder would project at about (1120, 450), 0.5 m from the lens: a soft near shape cutting into the lamp side that would tear in 2.5D parallax moves.
- By exact projection on 1280x720 (the same maths reproduces the current corners file to 0.1 px):
  - panel TL (268, 102), TR (675, 88), BR (673, 298), BL (294, 340). That is 17.7° off axis instead of 29°: the left edge is 238 px and the right 210 px, a 12 % keystone instead of 22 %.
  - the housing's top at y 75-88;
  - the lamp bulb at about (862, 236), so the shade is whole at about x 850-960, y 150-305. The camera sees its back: it is about 73° off the reflector axis, so no bare bulb shows.
  - the lamp's base at (792, 565) and the front edge of the monitor's foot at about x 430-595, y 545-585;
  - the steep near edge of the lamp's pool on the oak entering at the bottom right (about x 880-1210, y 620-720). The pad stays out of frame apart from its far corner.
- At an 8 % push about the frame centre, the housing's top stays 52 px from the edge.
- Remove the laptop first (fix 2). From this camera its lid would stand just under the housing, with its top edge at about y 375-460.
- Before rendering, check report_frame's log, sk.screen_frame_metadata and world_to_camera_view on 'lamp_bulb', 'monitor foot' and the pad.
- Accept when:
  - the monitor's foot meets visible wood with a contact shadow;
  - the lamp shade is whole and at least 60 px from every edge;
  - the housing is at least 60 px from every edge;
  - no object comes within 30 px of the bezel.

fixes.problem: The laptop stands between Tim's side of the desk and the monitor, and in this frame its lid hides the monitor's lower post and foot. From the fix 1 camera it would not block the panel: the sightlines to the panel pass 14-23 cm above the lid. But its top edge would project at about x 355-685, y 375-460, right under the housing's lower edge (y 311-357), and hide the post and foot again. Its screen faces +Y (turned -75°), toward both cameras, so it is a second lit screen in the cutaway. The two screens are 0.30 m apart and split the beat.
fixes.fix:
Make the monitor Tim's one screen:
- Remove st.group('laptop', st.laptop()) from build().
- apply_camera reads bpy.data.objects['laptop_screen'] without a check (the 'Screen backlight power' and emission-colour lines). Remove or guard those lines too, or the build fails.
- Drop 'laptop_screen_light' from TRIMS, and update the stage docstring.
- This also takes the lit lid edge out from behind his head in `window`, which r2 noted; there laptop_screen_light still runs at 0.25.
- If the lead wants a laptop kept, close it (lid shut, about 25 mm thick) and lay it on the desk clear of the monitor's foot. Keep it inside the desk's ends at x ±0.70. Check with a ray cast from each camera to the four panel corners and to the foot that nothing hits first, and that it stays at least 30 px from the foot and the housing in the monitor frame.

fixes.problem:
On the graded frame, about 7 % of the lit pixels outside the panel are warm (29 % raw). The causes:
- room_fill runs at x8.0 in the default blue (0.6, 0.72, 1.0), because room_fill_colour has no 'monitor' key.
- The slat exclusion applies only to 'window'.
- laptop_screen_light is 0.18.
The panel carries 76 % of the frame's light.

The plate has no glass and no coverage matte. The panel is bare emission (mt.glow), so a pinned insert will carry no reflection and look pasted on. Any insert darker than the panel will also show a faint light rim in the 1-2 px anti-aliased edge. On the graded JPEG the vignette makes the panel fall from about L 128 at its centre to about 80 at its top-left.
fixes.fix:
Publish two extra passes beside monitor.png, from the same camera, samples and pixel filter:
- monitor.mask.png, in the project's existing matte format (evidence_table's page.mask.png and pair.mask.png):
  - Set monitor_screen.pass_index = 1.
  - In install_hook, wrap the final 'monitor' render the way evidence_table.render_paper_mask does: Object Index pass, anti-aliased ID Mask, 8-bit BW PNG, ungraded.
  - The matte respects occlusion, so anything crossing the panel is cut out of it.
- monitor.glass.png:
  - Swap monitor_screen's material for mt.screen('monitor glass', (0, 0, 0), 0.0, 0.43, 0.43*9/16), a black glossy face (roughness 0.12, Specular IOR Level 0.35).
  - Its panel pixels then hold only the reflections of the room in front of the screen (the lamp and the lit desk), to add over the insert.
- Name both files in monitor.corners.json, with a note that the composite goes onto the raw PNG and the A-fixed grade (regrade_frames.sh) is applied afterwards.

fixes.problem:
Once the reframe shows the oak in front of the foot, the screen has to light it, and two things stop it:
- The panel material (mt.glow, emission 0.61 on (0.68, 0.75, 0.86)) has emission_sampling NONE, so its light reaches nearby surfaces only through BSDF-sampled paths.
- Unlike the laptop, it has no area light in front of it.
The current frame cannot show this, because nothing visible faces the panel (the wall, stool and blinds are behind it). The panel's brightness is right for the planned insert: in the current EDL_v3, shot 03-15 puts page 1 of Tim's written statement on it (s1_p1-1.png, mean 242/255).

fixes.fix:
After fixes 2-5, re-render desk, window and letters as finals at HEAD (1280x720, 1920x1080 for window, 64 spp) and republish them, with the monitor idle at 0.035.
- In `desk`, do not leave a sliver at the left edge. Panning the aim about 0.10 m toward +Y (image right) takes the housing fully out (its right edge to about x -18) while the lamp shade stays whole (bulb at about x 227). Re-check Tim's framing, which moves about 90 px left.
- In `window`:
  - check that his head clears the monitor's bezel by at least 40 px;
  - re-measure r2's acceptance numbers: at least 55 % of lit pixels warm, and the pool's mean at least 1.4 times the blinds'.

fixes.problem: The bezel's silhouette is weak. On the graded frame the left bezel is L 3-7 against the wall at 13-17. The right bezel (8-13) merges into the lamp arm (5-9 where they meet).
fixes.fix:
The reframe in fix 1 puts the blinds behind most of the housing and moves the lamp arm more than 100 px clear of the right bezel. In addition:
- In monitor(), lower the 'monitor charcoal housing' roughness from 0.46 to about 0.32. The housing's existing 6 mm bevels then catch the lamp and the spill as thin rims.
- Accept when every bezel edge differs from what lies behind it by at least 12 graded levels along at least 80 % of its length.
